draft.title: The vertebrate groups
card: Vertebrates are animals with a backbone. There are five groups: fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals.
Fish and amphibians
Fish have scales and breathe with gills, and they live in water. Amphibians have moist skin without scales. Young amphibians breathe with gills, and most adults breathe with lungs.
Reptiles and birds
Reptiles have dry scaly skin and breathe with lungs. Birds have feathers and breathe with lungs. Both reptiles and birds lay eggs with a hard or leathery shell.
Mammals
Mammals have hair or fur and breathe with lungs. Females feed their young with milk. Most mammals give birth to live young, but the platypus and echidna lay eggs.
draft.remember: Body covering, breathing and how young are born help tell the five vertebrate groups apart.

a.q: An animal has a backbone, feathers and lungs, and it lays eggs. Which group is it?
a.why: Feathers are found only in birds, so this animal is a bird. Reptiles also have lungs and lay eggs, but they have dry scaly skin, not feathers.
a.clue: Which group is the only one with feathers?

b.q: A scientist finds an animal in a Victorian creek. It has a backbone and moist skin with no scales. Its young breathe with gills and the adults breathe with lungs. Which group is it?
b.why: Moist skin with no scales, and young that breathe with gills while adults use lungs, match amphibians. Fish also breathe with gills, but they have scales and keep their gills as adults.
b.clue: Which group changes how it breathes as it grows?

problems.detail: 'Both reptiles and birds lay eggs with a hard or leathery shell' is false for many reptiles. Many Australian reptiles, including Victorian species such as the tiger snake, lowland copperhead and blue-tongue lizards, give birth to live young. Say 'most reptiles lay eggs'.
Why (a) says 'Reptiles also have lungs and lay eggs', which repeats the card's overgeneralisation that all reptiles lay eggs. Many Australian reptiles give birth to live young.
'Fish have scales' is an overgeneralisation. Some fish, such as many catfish and lampreys, have no scales. 'Most fish have scales' would be accurate.
